answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit a claim; a randomly selected set of peers then audits the claim against independent evidence. If an audit proves fabrication, the stake is slashed and paid to the auditors, while repeated claims from one identity do not increase its influence. A Sybil attacker must therefore acquire and risk real capital for every voting identity, and loses that capital when caught. A copper shipment recorded by yarrow growers in the grove can serve as a test claim.
